questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design a namespace-scoped TLS gateway leveraging CRD, InitContainer, Secrets, and a ready path tied to certificate availability.

## Key Concepts

- CustomResourceDefinition for per-namespace gateways
- InitContainer fetching TLS certs via Vault-like API
- Secrets mounted into gateway for TLS material
- Readiness/Liveness linked to cert presence/expiry; logs to a PVC

## Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: tlsgateways.example.com
spec:
  group: example.com
  versions:
  - name: v1
    served: true
    storage: true
    schema:
      openAPIV3Schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          spec:
            type: object
            properties:
              serviceName:
                type: string
              port:
                type: integer
              hostname:
                type: string
              apiTokenSecret:
                type: string
```

```yaml
apiVersion: example.com/v1
kind: TLSGateway
metadata:
  name: my-service-gateway
  namespace: default
spec:
  serviceName: my-service
  port: 443
  hostname: app.example.com
  apiTokenSecret: tlsgateway-token
```

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: tls-gateway
  namespace: default
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: tls-gateway
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: tls-gateway
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: fetch-certs
        image: curlimages/curl:8.1
        command: ["sh", "-c", "curl -sS http://vault.example/api/cert -o /certs/tls.crt"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: certs
          mountPath: /certs
      containers:
      - name: envoy
        image: envoyproxy/envoy:v1.23.0
        ports:
        - containerPort: 443
        volumeMounts:
        - name: certs
          mountPath: /etc/envoy/certs
      volumes:
      - name: certs
        secret:
          secretName: tlsgateway-certs
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you handle cert rotation cadence and revocation?
- What RBAC would you implement for the InitContainer to access the API token?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical use of NetworkPolicy to enforce zero-trust interactions between microservices and their dependents, a common production pattern.

## Key Concepts
- NetworkPolicy basics: podSelector, ingress/egress, policyTypes
- namespace-scoped rules and label selectors
- Egress to specific app Pods on defined ports
- Validation: simulate allowed and blocked traffic, inspect policy state

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: payment-allow
  namespace: finance
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: payment
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  - Egress
  ingress:
  - from:
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: frontend
  egress:
  - to:
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: db
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 5432
  - to:
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: cache
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 6379
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you adapt if payment also needs cross-namespace database access?
- What runtime and network-layer observability would you enable to detect policy violations?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Explores per-namespace data ingestion, config-driven parsing, and strict egress controls—core CKAD topics with practical trade-offs.

## Key Concepts
- ConfigMaps for runtime parsing rules
- PVC-backed logs and InitContainers for tooling
- Secrets for credentials and tokens
- TLS sidecar and cert rotation
- Readiness/Liveness probes
- Namespace NetworkPolicy egress controls

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal skeleton: Deployment, PVC, ConfigMap/Secret refs
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: log-router
  namespace: <namespace>
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: log-router
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: log-router
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: install-tools
        image: alpine:3.18
        command: ["/bin/sh","-c","apk add --no-cache awk sed curl"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: logs
          mountPath: /logs
      containers:
      - name: router
        image: myorg/log-router:latest
        env:
        - name: REGEX
          valueFrom:
            configMapKeyRef:
              name: log-config
              key: regex
        - name: BATCH_SIZE
          valueFrom:
            configMapKeyRef:
              name: log-config
              key: batchSize
        volumeMounts:
        - name: logs
          mountPath: /logs
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8080
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8080
      volumes:
      - name: logs
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: logs-pvc
      - name: tls
        secret:
          secretName: log-tls
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test the regex parsing and batching in a SRP-safe way?
- What metrics would you expose for reliability and observability?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests CKAD ability to compose a small, namespace-scoped verification workflow that touches ConfigMaps, Secrets, PVCs, and network policy.

## Key Concepts
- Deployment with InitContainer
- ConfigMap-based allowlist
- Secret-based credentials and TLS sidecar
- PVC-mounted /secrets and lightweight parsing with jq/yq
- Readiness/Liveness probes and per-namespace NetworkPolicy

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: compliance-api-creds
  namespace: default
data:
  token: <base64>
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: secret-allowlist
  namespace: default
data:
  allowed_keys: |
    tls.key
    tls.crt
    creds
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: secret-compliance-checker
  namespace: default
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: secret-compliance-checker
    spec:
      initContainers:
        - name: install-tools
          image: alpine:3.18
          command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache jq curl && wget -O - https://github.com/yq-dev/yq/releases/latest/download/yq_linux_amd64 -O /usr/local/bin/yq && chmod +x /usr/local/bin/yq"]
      containers:
        - name: checker
          image: alpine:3.18
          command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "./check.sh"]
          volumeMounts:
            - name: secrets
              mountPath: /secrets
      volumes:
        - name: secrets
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: secret-storage
      readinessProbe:
        httpGet:
          path: /healthz
          port: 8080
        initialDelaySeconds: 5
        periodSeconds: 10
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you scale and test this in a real cluster?
- What are risks with mounting Secrets in /secrets and how to mitigate?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests CKAD fundamentals for per-namespace automation, using CronJobs, ConfigMaps, Secrets, InitContainers, and PVC-backed logs in a realistic heartbeat scenario.

## Key Concepts

- CronJob scheduling and Job templates
- ConfigMap and Secret usage for config and creds
- InitContainer for one-time setup
- Probes for container health
- PersistentVolumeClaim for logs

## Code Example

```javascript
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: heartbeat-cron
  namespace: default
spec:
  schedule: "*/10 * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          initContainers:
          - name: install-deps
            image: alpine:3.19
            command: ["sh","-c","apk add --no-cache curl"]
          containers:
          - name: heartbeater
            image: alpine:3.19
            command: ["sh","-c","curl -sS -X POST -H \"Authorization: Bearer $API_TOKEN\" $TARGET_URL/heartbeat -d '{\"ts\": \"$(date +%s)\"}'"]
            envFrom:
            - configMapRef:
                name: cron-config
            - secretRef:
                name: target-creds
            volumeMounts:
            - name: logs
              mountPath: /logs
            readinessProbe:
              exec:
                command: ["sh","-c","test -f /logs/ready"]
              initialDelaySeconds: 5
              periodSeconds: 10
            livenessProbe:
              httpGet:
                path: /healthz
                port: 80
              initialDelaySeconds: 15
              periodSeconds: 20
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
          volumes:
          - name: logs
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: heartbeat-logs
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you rotate the API token without recreating the CronJob?
- What failure modes and retries would you implement?
